name: Emil Design Engineering
description: Applies deliberate motion, interaction timing and interface polish without sacrificing usability.
constraints: Motion must explain state, hierarchy or causality; do not animate merely to decorate.
Respect reduced-motion preferences and never delay essential actions for animation.
Avoid layout-triggering animation when transform or opacity can express the same transition.
guidance: Choose duration and easing from the interaction: entrances settle, exits leave quickly and direct manipulation follows the pointer.
Use motion to preserve spatial continuity and show where content came from or went.
Keep microinteractions short, interruptible and consistent across components.
Prefer transform and opacity, and verify the final semantic state after rapid repeated input.
Polish typography, spacing, borders and shadows together with motion rather than treating animation as a separate layer.
completion_checks: Every animation has a functional reason and consistent timing.
The interface remains complete and understandable with reduced motion enabled.
Rapid or interrupted interactions end in the correct visual and semantic state.
Motion does not create layout shift, blocked input or avoidable performance work.
